CYCLE 10 PAIRWISE HEIGHT-POTENTIAL AUDIT
Worker: cycle10_recovery_duality_luna, Luna/max
Scope: test whether center-dependent recentered fits admit a stationarity-based two-point potential estimate at the critical center dimension s=m-1. This is a local obstruction search, not an acquired lemma or an ambient regularity proof.

Result. The proposed unweighted estimate

  integral_{x in C} integral |z_x(y)| |x-y|^{-m} dmu(y) dsigma(x)
      <= C * normalized_excess

is false even for an actual stationary integral varifold satisfying the near-flat, Q=2 density-center, and local-fit interface. A small-angle crossing of two planes gives a left side of order theta while the normalized tilt, projected-mass, and squared-height excess is order theta^2. The model has one common exact minimal reference through every center, so it does not refute a tilt-weighted estimate for genuinely center-dependent references.

The radial error that generated the critical endpoint contains the squared tilt e_x. Retaining the height gives the correct first candidate

  P_i(l) = integral_{x in C_i} integral_{B_{Cl}(x)}
             e_{i,x}(y) |z_{i,x}(y)| |x-y|^{-m}
             dmu_i(y) dsigma_i(x),

not the unweighted potential. Logarithmic scale integration also produces a second kernel

  K_m(r,l) = integral_{r/C}^l t^{1-m} dt

against e_{i,x}; it is O(l) for m=1, log(Cl/r) for m=2, and O(r^{2-m}) for m>2. Under the critical Frostman bound sigma_i(B_t)<=C t^{m-1} and the recentering estimate e_{i,x}<=C(e_i+a_i^2), this second term is bounded by C l a_i^2 using the local mass/tilt budget. The first term is the only logarithmic obstruction.

If all centers lie on one common minimal S and the same S is used for every center, then z_x(y)=z(y), |z(y)|<=dist(y,C_i), and the critical Riesz potential of sigma_i is at most C/dist(y,C_i). This gives P_i(l)<=C integral e_i dmu_i<=C a_i^2. That is the exact common-base cancellation from the earlier frozen packet. It is not available for recentered fits that vary with x. The fitting inputs currently give only a local |z_{i,x}(y)|<=C|x-y| bound and the global energy budget; those two estimates leave a logarithm in the pairwise potential. No stationarity estimate controlling that logarithm was acquired here.

The local fitting overlap result compares two centered fits with the moment, tilt, and mass conclusions. It explicitly does not apply autom

CYCLE 10 TILT-WEIGHTED CENTER POTENTIAL AUDIT
Worker: cycle10_nonlinear_dynamics_luna, Luna/max
Scope: exact center-fit transition and stationarity reduction for
  P_i(l)=int_{x in C_i} int e_{i,x}(y)|z_{i,x}(y)| |x-y|^{-m} dmu_i(y) dsigma_i(x).
Status: exact reduction proved in the affine-reference model; the required
cubic-potential estimate is not proved from the pinned fitting hypotheses.
No earlier frozen file was edited. No new abstract rectifiability proof was read.

RESULT

There is an exact stationarity identity that retains the height and tilt in
the desired product. In the flat codimension-one model, let h be signed
height above a fixed affine plane and let each centered fit be its parallel
translate through x. Then

  z_x(y)=h(y)-h(x),       e_x(y)=|grad_{T_y V} h|^2,

and, for any compactly supported annular kernel K(x,y),

  2 int K |z_x| e_x dmu
       = - int z_x|z_x| <grad_T K, grad_T h> dmu.

Dyadic annular decomposition and Cauchy-Schwarz give the precise reduction

  P(l) <= C H(l),
  H(l)=int_C int_{B_{Cl}(x)} |z_x(y)|^3 |x-y|^{-m-2} dmu(y) dsigma(x).

Thus the weighted term is controlled if the cubic pair-height potential H
has the required a_i^2 (or o(a_i^2)/eta_i) bound. This is a stationarity
identity, not a generic Dini assertion. The remaining H bound is not a
consequence of the currently listed global mass/height/tilt budgets by any
argument established here.

The center-dependent fits have an exact additive transition in flat graph
coordinates. If S_x is obtained by translating a fixed graph S_0 through
the center x, and u is support height relative to S_0, then

  z_x(y)=u(y)-u(x),
  z_x(y)-z_{x'}(y)=u(x')-u(x).

For the fixed-domain near-flat Dirichlet recentering family
S_c=graph(f+c+v_c), v_0=0, ||D_c v_c||_{C^1}<=C eps_i, this becomes

  z_x(y)=u(y)-u(x)+v_{c_x}(b_x)-v_{c_x}(b_y),
  |v_{c_x}(b_x)-v_{c_x}(b_y)|<=C eps_i a_i |b_x-b_y|,

in the fixed graph coordinates, where u is the old-reference height,
b_x,b_y are horizontal projections, and |c_x|<=C a_i. The transition
remainders are an additive cocycle because they are differences of the same
graphs. This supplies coherence without identifying all S_x with one fit.
It does not provide a square-function bound for u(x')-u(x).

EARLY FALSIFIER: A FIRST-ORDER AFFINE TRANSITION IS REAL

In R^3 take the stationary integral varifold V=Q|P_beta|, where
P_beta={(s,t,z): z=beta s},
